title: Reconciler: repair stuck factory states on every sweep
body:
## Parent

Spec: #9 (software factory v0 on chronicle). Glossary: CONTEXT.md.

## What to build

The factory must never wait forever on a lost event. Today every transition is event-driven (a label, a PR event, a push) and a missed or cancelled event leaves a ticket or PR stranded until a human notices. The dispatcher's schedule job becomes a reconciler: on every sweep it reads real state and repairs anything past its deadline, so a lost event costs at most one sweep.

Stuck states to detect, each with a deadline and a repair, all as a pure unit-tested decision over fixture data (labels, run list, PR checks, timestamps in; actions out):

- A ticket carrying `agent:implement` or `agent:in-progress` with no live or recent run: re-add `agent:implement` (with FACTORY_PAT so the event fires); after a second miss, escalate to `needs-human` with a comment.
- A PR carrying `agent:review` with no live or recent review run: re-add the label; second miss escalates.
- An open factory PR with auto-merge armed and no `factory/verdict` status after its deadline: re-add `agent:review`.
- An open factory PR whose head is behind main and whose update-branch never ran: call update-branch.
- A ticket in `agent:in-progress` whose only run was cancelled by slot contention: re-add `agent:implement`.

Deadlines are inputs with defaults. Each repair is logged with the reason so the run log reads as a list of decisions. Repairs are idempotent: running the sweep twice changes nothing the second time.

GitHub's cron is unreliable on this account (the fixture saw a seven hour gap on 2026-09-07). Add a documented external trigger: the sweep also runs on `repository_dispatch` with a named event type, and the README shows a one-line `gh api` call a cron on any machine can send, so the sweep does not depend on GitHub's scheduler.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A fixture ticket left in `agent:in-progress` with no run is re-dispatched by the next sweep, and escalated to `needs-human` after the second miss
- [ ] A fixture PR with `agent:review` and no run is re-reviewed by the next sweep
- [ ] A fixture PR with auto-merge armed and no verdict past the deadline gets a review run from the sweep
- [ ] A sweep over a healthy fixture makes no changes, and running it twice in a row makes none
- [ ] The decision function has node --test unit tests over fixture states, no network
- [ ] The sweep runs on `repository_dispatch` from outside GitHub, proven with one call from a local machine
- [ ] Every repair is a logged decision naming the state, the deadline, and the action

## Blocked by

- None (can start immediately). Recommended before #20.

title: gh helpers: 64 MB maxBuffer, the reconciler died with ENOBUFS on a busy repo (#19)
body:
During the #19 attempt-2 run the cron sweep (factory-fixture run 34158133968, 20:06Z) failed in the reconciler with `Error: spawnSync gh ENOBUFS`: the paginated runs listing for a repo with 80+ runs in the window passed Node's 1 MB default maxBuffer. The dispatcher half had finished; the event path drove every state, so the proof was unaffected, but the safety net was down.

- 64 MB maxBuffer on the four `gh` helpers (sweep, dispatch, update-branch, shared common)
- no behaviour change otherwise; 227 tests green
